verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same norm, encoded as one supremum instead of a max of sups. Term by term: the paper's R = [X0,X1] x [-1,1] is Icc X₀ X₁ times J = Icc (-1) 1; the paper's max over 0 <= r <= j and sup over R is Lean's single sSup over the set of all values ‖iteratedFDerivWithin ℝ n (f i X) J η‖ with n ≤ k, X ∈ Icc X₀ X₁, η ∈ J (a sup of sups equals the sup over the union); the paper's "maximum of the component norms for tuples" is the extra index i : Fin m inside the same set. The eta-derivative is taken within J at fixed X, so derivatives at η = ±1 are one-sided, as the paper requires, and no radial derivative is taken. Two encoding choices: (a) Lean adjoins the element 0 to the set, which only guarantees nonemptiness and nonnegativity and does not change the value, since the paper's quantity is already a sup of absolute values over a nonempty rectangle; (b) ‖iteratedFDerivWithin ℝ n g J η‖ is the operator norm of the n-th iterated Fréchet derivative, which for a real function of one real variable equals |∂^n_η g| (standard Mathlib isometry). Lean's sSup also returns the junk value 0 for an unbounded set, where the paper's sup would be +∞; in the one place the definition is used (profile_comparison_norm) the jet-bound hypotheses make every such set bounded (jetValues_bddAbove, parameterNorm_bounds), so no vacuity arises there.
